text:
oncall-bot: 🔔 ALERT: increased connection resets and egress errors measured from us-east-1a (subnet 172.31.48.0/24). p95 token latency 450ms, 5xx spike to 2.8%. auto-metrics flagged at 2019-12-05T14:09UTC.

michael: seeing the same in traces — a subset of AZ egress appears to be blackholing outbound connections. internal NAT retries 504s.

sara: confirming packet loss on BGP peer to our egress provider in us-east-1a. Not all hosts, looks subnet-scoped.

jin: are other AZs in us-east-1 healthy? what's capacity to absorb traffic if we shift?

sara: us-east-1b/c healthy but GPU pools in 1b at ~72% and 1c at ~66%. We can absorb some but not full traffic. Cross-region to eu-west-1 or na-west will add egress cost and latency.

ali: TL;DR: need soft failover to avoid large cache churn and sudden token cost blowups. propose incremental weight shift off us-east-1a -> 1b and 1c first (up to 30%), then spill to other regions if errors persist.

michael: agree. also want to avoid saturating 1b GPU pools — suggest staging 20% now, monitor 15m, then +10% if error rate still >1%.

jin: happy with that. I'll run a gradual GSLB weight update with a 5m ramp per step. Command below:

```
# do not copy to public, internal cli
redwood-gslb adjust-weight --route api.redwood.ai --from az=us-east-1a --to azs=us-east-1b,us-east-1c --percent=20 --ramp-seconds=300 --note "soft-failover us-east-1a egress blackhole"
```

ali: also adding a precautionary rule to route new sessions preferentially to same-region AZs to reduce cross-region egress. If we must cross-region, prefer na-west over eu due to lower latency for most customers.

sara: monitoring GPU scheduler in 1b/1c. If queue depth > 120ms or GPU utilization > 80% for 2 consecutive polls, abort further shifts and open an ops incident.

michael: set alert for per-region spool queue and token cost delta. Who will hit the button?

jin: I'll run the first 20% adjustment now.

oncall-bot: ACTION: change requested by jin. Recording change id change-20230314-1021.

jin: executed step 1 -> 20% shift off us-east-1a to 1b/1c with 5m ramp.

michael: initial metrics: errors down from 2.8% to 1.5% after 4m, p95 latency improved ~70ms. GPU 1b util jumped to 78%.

sara: GPU 1b now 82% on a few hosts, moving some inference groups to 1c to rebalance.

ali: recommend we freeze cross-region spill for now, keep within same region. cost trade-off not worth it unless full AZ outage.

jin: agree. holding at 20% for 15m; next action depends on errors <1% and GPU queue <100ms.

michael: note — if errors trend down and latency stabilizes, we should plan a controlled revert later once provider resolves peering. Revert plan: mirror steps in reverse over 30m.

sara: filing ticket with egress provider (case #EG-4823). They see flaps on their edge router to that subnet. ETA unknown.

ali: recording decision: soft-failover 20% to us-east-1b/c, hold, monitor 15m, don't cross-region unless >80% error. Cost owner: finance@redwood for egress cost variance.

michael: thanks team. watching dashboards; ping here with any spike.

oncall-bot: UPDATE: change change-20230314-1021 succeeded. Post-change snapshot saved to /ops/changes/20230314/change-20230314-1021.json

jin: follow-up after 18m: errors now 0.9% and p95 stable. GPU 1b steady 79%, 1c 68%. Holding.

sara: provider acknowledged issue and set a maintenance window to reroute peering in ~2h. We'll coordinate revert after they confirm fix.

ali: good runbook note — when reverting, use a slower ramp (600s) to avoid cache invalidation and token surge. Also pre-warm KV cache where possible for high-affinity customers.

michael: closing thread for now. reopen if errors >1% or any host-level GPU OOMs. Great run. :thumbsup:
